evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 字形; 形義通解; 《說文》; 《詩》; 《公羊傳》
evidence.text: The entry displays one small-seal form, one bronze example, and four manuscript examples; it displays no oracle-bone example. Its account analyzes the bronze form as 水 plus sound element 曷 and says 渴 was an older graph for 竭 in “water dried up/exhausted” contexts, citing the Zhongshan King Fanghu and a Mawangdui Laozi manuscript. It quotes Shuowen’s 盡也 and 从水、曷聲. Separately it cites the Shijing line 苟無飢渴 for thirst, a Tang Bai Juyi example for dry/parched, and a Gongyang zhuan use glossed “urgent.” These are the database’s interpretations and citations; they do not establish every semantic bridge or the earliest surviving physical witness of the Shijing line.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 渴

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: The entry quotes 渴, 盡也, 从水、曷聲, and lists Guangyun fanqie 苦曷 and 渠列 with distinct Middle Chinese categories. It identifies a bronze 渴 graph as used for 竭 and cites the Fanghu phrase 渴(竭)志盡忠. This is the database’s paleographic and lexicographic account, not an independent photograph-based verification in this research.

evidence.text: Attempted the official per-character Unihan lookups for 渴 (U+6E34), 曷 (U+66F7), and 氵 (U+6C35); each endpoint was inaccessible. Local rows supplied in the input report kě, hé, and shui respectively, and local Baxter–Sagart rows report 渴 *Nə-[k]ʰˤat (MC khat) and 曷 *[g]ˤat (MC hat). These local readings retain their supplied notation; they show overlapping final/coda material and distinct initials in Baxter–Sagart, but do not independently prove a phonetic role. No verified external character page was obtained for the three Unihan values.

evidence.source: 臺灣教育部《異體字字典》
evidence.field: 說文釋形; readings and definitions; shape records
evidence.text: The entry quotes Shuowen’s “盡也。从水，曷聲” and gives separate readings and glosses: jié for dried up/exhausted, kě for thirst and urgency, and hé for a Chu-Yue regional term for reverse-flowing water. It lists a Shuowen Da-Xu small-seal item; several bronze-script compilations are marked unavailable on this entry. This is lexicographic evidence, not an independently inspected bronze image.
evidence.title: [A02267] 渴 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: Dong Chinese analyzes 氵 as the meaning component and 曷 as the sound component; it calls 氵 a component form of 水 and labels displayed 渴 forms bronze script (Late Warring States, about 250 BCE), Shuowen seal script (about 100 CE), and Eastern Han clerical script. It gives 渴 *Nə-[k]ʰˤat and 曷 *[g]ˤat in Baxter–Sagart notation. Those dates and readings are secondary-source assertions; the ancient forms were not independently visually inspected here.
evidence.title: 渴 - Dong Chinese dictionary

evidence.field: 曷 graphic origin; Shuowen; sound-component listings
evidence.text: Dong Chinese proposes that 曷 depicted cut fruit and that the current interrogative use is a phonetic loan. It also gives 曷 *[g]ˤat, Middle Chinese hat, hé, lists it as a sound component in 渴, and quotes Shuowen’s 从曰、匃聲. The cut-fruit referent is not independently established by the sources inspected here; uncertainty about that proposed original referent does not itself negate 曷’s later role as a sound component in 渴.
evidence.kind: secondary character dictionary; disputed graphic-origin proposal
evidence.title: 曷 - Dong Chinese dictionary

evidence.field: Zhongshan Fanghu text and date context
evidence.text: The transcription includes 貫渴（竭）志盡忠 in search-extracted text. It supports a reading glossed with 竭 but its garbled opened PDF text does not show the precise inscribed graph. CUHK supplies the claim that the graph was 渴. The transcription alone therefore cannot independently confirm the graph identification.
evidence.kind: museum-hosted inscription transcription; text extraction limited
evidence.title: 中山王譬壺 (PDF transcription)

evidence.text: The inspected U+6E34 record reports Pinyin kě and the definition “thirsty, parched; yearn, pine.” It also displays a kMandarin value of kě. This secondary Unicode-data aggregator independently confirms only 渴’s current value here; exact official per-character pages for 曷 and 氵 remained inaccessible.

search_audit.outcome: Inspected Dong Chinese entries for 渴 and 曷 and the secondary U+6E34 Unicode-data page, which reports kě. The corresponding 曷 and 氵 aggregator pages and official per-character Unihan endpoints were inaccessible.

gaps: No glyph image is selected. The exact Commons page, official imageinfo API, and SVG were attempted but inaccessible; candidate identity, pixels, provenance, and rights were not independently verified.

Exact official Unihan character pages for 渴, 曷, and 氵 could not be opened. Local rows were supplied in the input; a secondary U+6E34 page confirms 渴 kě, but external character-specific readings for 曷 hé and 氵 shui were not verified.

The supplied Baxter–Sagart rows show 渴 *Nə-[k]ʰˤat (MC khat) and 曷 *[g]ˤat (MC hat), with different initials but overlapping final/coda material. The upstream reconstruction PDF was not successfully inspected in this invocation; the local rows are not external evidence.
CUHK reports no oracle-bone example in its displayed 渴 entry; this does not establish absence from every oracle-bone corpus. The source’s glyph images were not visually inspected here.

CUHK reports a bronze use of 渴 for 竭, but the opened inscription transcription renders 竭 and does not independently show the graph’s shape. Its specific graph identification remains attributed to CUHK.

The semantic development from “exhausted/dried up” to “thirsty/parched” is plausible but no dated bridging stages were verified. The earliest physical witness for the cited Shijing line was not established; the character’s semantic chronology cannot be inferred from the cited gloss list.
The precise graphic transition from full 水 in the reported bronze analysis to the modern left-side 氵 is not traced by the inspected sources. No distinct origin_form relationship is assigned to 氵.
Dong Chinese’s proposed cut-fruit origin for 曷 is not independently established. Its uncertain original depicted referent remains separate from the documented traditional phonetic analysis within 渴.
No small tracked extract is recommended: reuse terms for the recurring character-specific research material were not verified.
